security_spec.violation_condition: When the kernel enables qspinlocks based on Ziccrse detection (RISCV_QUEUED_SPINLOCKS or RISCV_COMBO_SPINLOCKS with ziccrse available) and schedules a spinlock holder onto a hart whose coherent cacheable main memory PMA region lacks RsrvEventual support, the LR/SC in cmpxchg may never make forward progress, causing the unlock path to livelock indefinitely.
security_spec.summary: Ziccrse now formally requires RsrvEventual on coherent cacheable main memory; kernel qspinlocks implicitly depend on this guarantee but do not verify per-PMA-region reservability at runtime, so a firmware/hardware PMA misconfiguration could cause silent hart-level livelock.

findings.finding: The kernel enables queued spinlocks solely based on ZICCRSE ISA string presence (line 297), without verifying the RsrvEventual PMA property that Ziccrse requires for its forward-progress guarantee. On a platform where M-mode firmware configures main memory without RsrvEventual, the LR/SC-based cmpxchg in qspinlock fast/slow paths can livelock indefinitely because lr.w reservation may never succeed. The kernel has no SBI mechanism to query PMA properties, so this gap is architectural — but it means the Ziccrse check alone is insufficient to guarantee correctness.

When Zacas is unavailable (no amocas), cmpxchg on RISC-V falls back to a plain lr.w/sc.w retry loop (lines 199-207). On a hart whose PMA region lacks RsrvEventual, this loop may spin forever. When qspinlocks are enabled based on Ziccrse detection, the fast-path lock acquisition (queued_spin_lock → atomic_try_cmpxchg_acquire → arch_cmpxchg_acquire) and slow-path queue transitions (atomic_try_cmpxchg_relaxed in xchg_tail when _Q_PENDING_BITS != 8) both execute this same LR/SC retry loop. With Ziccrse but no RsrvEventual, Ziccrse's forward-progress guarantee is voided.

The combo-spinlock dispatch (arch_spin_lock/unlock at line 26) resolves at runtime via static_branch_unlikely(&qspinlock_key). There is no per-hart check: if qspinlock_key is enabled because CPU0 detected Ziccrse, all harts use qspinlocks even if a hotplugged CPU's PMA regions lack RsrvEventual. The queued_spin_unlock path (include/asm-generic/qspinlock.h:128) uses smp_store_release on lock->locked — a plain store, no LR/SC — so unlock itself won't livelock. But the holder of a lock queued behind a stuck LR/SC on another hart may never get the lock.

RISCV_QUEUED_SPINLOCKS depends on NONPORTABLE (line 518). Its help text states that LR/SC with Ziccrse provides the forward-progress guarantee (line 522-523), but there is no Kconfig dependency on Ziccrse, no runtime ISA check (it unconditionally uses qspinlocks), and no mention of the RsrvEventual PMA dependency. A user building a NONPORTABLE kernel with this option on Ziccrse-but-no-RsrvEventual hardware gets a silently broken spinlock implementation.
findings.snippet:
config RISCV_QUEUED_SPINLOCKS
    bool "Using queued spinlock"
    depends on SMP && MMU && NONPORTABLE
    select ARCH_USE_QUEUED_SPINLOCKS
    help
      The queued spinlock implementation requires the forward progress
      guarantee of cmpxchg()/xchg() atomic operations: CAS with Zabha or
      LR/SC with Ziccrse provide such guarantee.

findings.finding: When CONFIG_RISCV_TICKET_SPINLOCKS is selected, the function returns early and never enables qspinlocks. Ticket spinlocks on RISC-V use AMO-based fetch-and-add (amoadd.w) for lock acquisition and plain stores for unlock — no LR/SC dependency, therefore no RsrvEventual requirement. This path is safe.

qspinlock_key defaults to true (DEFINE_STATIC_KEY_TRUE) under CONFIG_RISCV_COMBO_SPINLOCKS only. The key is disabled in riscv_spinlock_init when neither Zabha+Zacas nor Ziccrse is available (line 302). The default-true design is safe because the disable path runs before any spinlock user — riscv_spinlock_init is called from setup_arch at line 343, before SMP bringup.

Ziccrse is registered with __RISCV_ISA_EXT_DATA (no validation callback), matching the design that Ziccrse is a pure ISA-string property with no enable/disable side effects in S-mode. The extension detection is correct; the gap is in the consumer (riscv_spinlock_init) which doesn't account for the PMA dependency.
